profile.headline: Software Engineer, UX Designer, Problem Solver
profile.summary:
Hey there! I’m Brenna - thanks for stopping by my page. I’m a software developer, Rhode Islander, animal lover, gamer, and most importantly - human! I’ve spent the last 9 years at IBM, first as an intern then as a developer for IBM Order Management Software and am currently a front end developer at Marstone Inc. 

I find it satisfying and rewarding to create an experience that helps the greatest number of people. I’m curious about how modern tools and technology, such as AI, VR and AR, will continue to integrate our everyday lives. What will the future of human-tech relations look like? How can we create tools and experiences that adapt to the needs of the customers, industry, and modern society? And how can we continuously adapt in a responsible, ethical, and equitable way?

In my opinion, the most exciting thing about working in technology is that my dream job probably doesn’t exist yet. Every day I’m learning and preparing for the opportunity that may lead me to *that thing* which turns my job into my calling.

Actively upskilling and looking for new opportunities so please free to email me at brennacclark@gmail.com!

positions.title: AV/IT Tech
positions.description: As a technician serving at corporate event venues like the Boston Convention and Exhibition Center and Amica Mutual Pavilion. I am responsible for installing, configuring, and maintaining computer systems, networking, and AV equipment. My duties also include diagnosing and resolving technical issues with AV equipment and computer systems. I conduct regular system tests to ensure the quality and reliability of our setups. Additionally, I am tasked with communicating technical issues and providing status updates to clients or team members. I also recommend upgrades or changes that could improve system performance and enhance the user experience.
positions.insights: Skills: Audio Visual Support · Troubleshooting · IT · Creative Problem Solving

projects.title: Sailbot 2013
projects.description:
Coordinated with a team of 10 computer science majors to design and build an autonomous robotic sailboat and enter it in the 2013 Sailbot competition.

Designed the artificial intelligence algorithms to calculate the angle of sail from the wind vane and communicate it to the rudder. Helped implement several important components of the physical boat including the wind vane and the anemometer. Explained the mathematical concepts of sailing to other teammates.

Steered the boat to first place in the manual control fleet race portion of the tournament. 

Came in 5th overall (out of 9 schools in the 1-meter class). Also received the award for least expensive boat.
